title: flatten collapses one level of a nested Result and keeps the inner failure in the combined error channel
notes: 01-result-lifting/result-tap-and-tap-error-observe-without-changing pins the observation members; this pins the one transformation member that was implemented and unreachable. `flatten` has existed on the runtime (poc/src/runtime/result.ts) with its own tests since before this case, and no `.sm` program could call it, because the member set an authored program may use is fixed by the checker prelude and the ownership walk's discharge set in poc/src/language/semantic.ts and neither had learned it. The refusal was not the obvious one: an undeclared member leaves the Result unconsumed, so the analyzer reported SMITHERS1301 and returned before the emitted TypeScript could report an unknown property — which is why a member can be implemented, tested, documented as required, and unreachable, without any gate going red. THE SECOND LINE IS THE POINT. `Result.try(() => lookup("zoe"))` is Ok(Err(Missing)), not Err: the body returns a Result rather than throwing, so the nesting is real and the inner failure is one level down. `no entry for zoe` proves flatten returned the INNER Result rather than the outer success, and the `Panic | Missing` error channel that reaches `.match` proves the two failure channels were combined rather than one of them dropped. `Result.try` over a Result-returning body is the authored form that builds the nesting at all; specification/failures.mdx §Authorability notes that `!` cannot produce it, since `!` marks its own output as a plain value.

xfail.reason: MEASURED 2026-08-28 through `run.mjs --backend both --filter result-flatten-collapses`, not assumed: the fork REFUSES this program with [SMITHERS1301@15:19, SMITHERS1301@16:18] — 'Result value is not consumed' — while the reference accepts it and prints both lines. Both backends carry their own copy of the discharge set and the fork's has not learned `flatten`: `compiler/forkbridge/lowering.go.txt` declares `resultConsumerMembers` as the same eleven names the reference used to hard-code, and its `SmithersOk`/`SmithersErr` prelude classes implement those eleven and no more. So the fix on the fork side is TWO edits, not one, and its own integrity assertion says so: `len(resultConsumerDecls) != 2*len(resultConsumerMembers)` refuses to start unless BOTH classes declare every listed name. This is fail-CLOSED — the fork rejects a valid program rather than running an invalid one — so the row is a reachability gap, not a soundness hole. Retire this marker when the fork's list and its two prelude classes learn `flatten`; the reference reached it by deriving both of its walks from one table (RESULT_MEMBER_SIGNATURES in poc/src/language/semantic.ts) so that a member cannot be declared and not admitted again.
xfail.doc: specification/failures.mdx, "Matching and Transformation", lists the required transformation and sequencing members as `map mapError andThen andThenAsync flatten`. The list is a direction obligation on an implementation, and `flatten` is on it.
